columns.description: Expense Description published for admin spend above £25,000 only

e7e4bb2c53fa19137a9bf142a3c2a65bbcb46bbb.notes: Used the recorded row-0 header, which gives clean full column names. But sample_rows show, right after it, a month-label line ('Apr-12', mostly blank) and then a second, messier repeated header line ('Supplier Name\n', 'Amount ', 'Expenses Type \n' appearing twice, trailing newlines) before real data resumes at 'DFID, DFID, 11/04/2012...'. This looks like a file made by concatenating monthly export blocks, each carrying its own divider/header lines as literal rows. A naive header_row=0 read will pull in these divider and repeated-header rows as fake data throughout the file (this pattern likely repeats every month) — reviewer/build step must filter out embedded label and header-repeat rows before loading. 'description' is only populated for admin spend above £25,000, so it will be sparse/mostly empty.

420e4dfec39b7560c4f8c1bda2106b2403f53bbb.notes: 'Allocation Date' is the only date column available; mapped to payment_date but it may represent an allocation/posting date rather than the actual payment date — reviewer should confirm.

61082d3b945a710929a8afb45534c638cbedc5bd.notes: 'amount' appears to be the net (pre-VAT) figure — sample rows show a separate 'vat' column at ~20% of 'amount' (e.g. amount 1960.0, vat 392.0). 'vat' and 'vat_code' are not mapped, per the rule against folding VAT into amount_gbp. 'beneficiary' is sometimes 'Redacted' in the sample rows; kept as published.

constants.body: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

950a0eb554e268731a52bd54a0522851c484878c.notes: Clean, single-header table; no issues noted.

1ba80a36fb5ae80e4ffccb4eed076ccc6823c56e.notes: Table also carries 'Organisational unit' (a directorate-level field, e.g. 'People Directorate') and 'Expenditure category' (a broader category than 'Detailed Expenses type', e.g. 'Supplies and Services') — only one column each is allowed for expense_area/expense_type, so these two were left unmapped; reviewer should check whether they'd be preferred over 'Service label'/'Detailed Expenses type'. 'Capital/\nRevenue' and 'Supplier ID' also unmapped, no schema slot for them.

c6c424dd880387e6be0a6acb0d0d1019472f080b.reject: Every sample row has 'Supplier Name' populated as 'BARCLAYCARD PROCUREMENT CARD' with the same 'Voucher' number, split across many small (including negative) amounts by expense type/area — this is a procurement-card (GPC) statement broken out by spend category, not supplier-level payment lines.

72175dccca39317a7c9c1ffc062126da64e95bfa.notes: Minimal 3-column table (Supplier, Payment Date, Amount only); no expense_area/expense_type/reference/description/period available.

aaaccba426aa5dc5457beb961c1450997e9e8d42.notes: Minimal 3-column table (Supplier, Payment Date, Amount only), same shape as the other Greenwich source in this family; no expense_area/expense_type/reference/description/period available.

96b0ed3d29dc9c851645931d1c19da57798a8c23.notes: File starts with a title line ('Wales Office spend over £500', 'May-10' ...) at row 0, a blank row at row 1, then the real header (ENTITY, EXPENSE_AREA, PAYMENT_DATE, PAYMENT_NUMBER, SUPPLIER_NAME, INVOICE_AMOUNT, NAC_DESCRIPTION, Service provided) at row 2 — header_row set to 2 accordingly. Reviewer should confirm the blank-row count is consistent for other months' files in this same series if more get added later.

bb1de01354561410818f817c8def9bf5889d3365.notes: File starts with a title line ('Payments for Publishing for Invoices paid between 01-SEP-2022 and 30-SEP-2022') at row 0, real header at row 1 — header_row set to 1 accordingly. Note the exact header text for payment_date and expense_area carries a leading space (' Paid Date', ' Department') in the source. 'Cost Centre' holds a code (e.g. 'D2510'), not a text description, but it is the only expense-type-like field available; reviewer should sanity-check this choice. 'Irrecoverable VAT' is present but not mapped to amount_gbp, per the rule against folding VAT into the payment amount.
